about.title: Personal Injury Help in Costa Mesa, California
about.longDescription: Costa Mesa sits where two heavily traveled routes meet, and the public record reflects that. In 2025, the city's final count showed 619 injury collisions, 847 people hurt, and 4 traffic deaths. The highest collision volumes were logged along Newport Boulevard, Harbor Boulevard, and both directions of SR-55, with reported crashes tending to cluster on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., when the afternoon commute and weekend traffic overlap. A collision is only one way to get hurt here. A slip inside a shop off Harbor, a dog bite on a neighborhood walk, a cyclist clipped at a driveway, or a wreck with a delivery van can all leave you juggling medical bills and missed paychecks at once. We handle personal injury claims for Costa Mesa and the wider Orange County area. Our team works on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery. Reaching out costs nothing, and you can decide whether to move forward after you've talked things through with us.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Costa Mesa Claim

items.title: You generally have two years, but not always
items.desc: California gives most injury claims a two-year filing window. Claims against a city, county, or state agency can require notice in as little as six months, so it pays to act early.

items.title: Partial fault doesn't shut you out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you share some blame for a crash on Newport Boulevard, your recovery is reduced by your percentage, not erased.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering in ordinary cases
items.desc: For typical injury claims in California, there is no statutory ceiling on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life.

items.title: Contingency means no upfront cost
items.desc: Our team works on contingency. You pay no fee unless there is a recovery, and contacting us is always free.

items.question: Where do collisions in Costa Mesa tend to occur, according to public records?
items.answer: The 2025 public-record counts show the highest collision volumes along Newport Boulevard, Harbor Boulevard, and SR-55 in both the northbound and southbound directions. Reported crashes tend to peak on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. These are neutral counts that reflect traffic volume and reporting, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Costa Mesa?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims in California, the deadline is two years from the date of injury. If a government entity is involved, such as a city vehicle or a public sidewalk, you may need to file a claim within six months. We can help you sort out which deadline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means sharing blame reduces your recovery rather than eliminating it. If you were found 25 percent responsible, for example, your compensation would be reduced by that share. Many people assume they have no claim when they actually do.
